scope: Independent review of the rejected v3/v4 CPU experiments and the final restored production core, plus restored r17 empty-slot SDI and compatibility boundaries.

checked_facts: SDICON bit 0 selects MMC/SD clock type; it is not a clock-enable bit.
CmdSent is independent of response receipt; command response timeout is 64 SDCLK periods.

support_boundaries: Empty SD slot only; no populated-card FIFO, sector transfer or DMA support.
NOR program and erase remain unsupported.
Functional clock equivalence is not electrical or cycle-accurate hardware validation.
Accepting both vendor-documented MAXP layouts does not establish physical aliasing.

rejected_candidate_review.reason: Default-browser throughput regression in the performance agent isolated measurement.

caller_constraints: exactly one CPU slot per quantum
more than one transition-free peripheral tick remains
no accepted pending FIQ or IRQ
continuing_paths: conservatively classified data processing without CPSR mode/mask change
required_boundaries: Every instruction fetch still performs translation and physical read after its own tick.
MMIO fetch, page-table read and data access synchronize deferred peripheral time and clear the quiet interval.
MSR, CP15, BX, Thumb, SPSR return, block transfers and other complex instructions return to the outer loop.
Data aborts and diagnostic stops return immediately before another instruction.
A successful store affects the next instruction fetch and page-table walk; no prefetched or decoded instruction survives.
directed_tests_reviewed: dependent ALU/condition chains with random public budget partitions
last mapped instruction before fetch abort
store rewriting next opcode through exact or mirrored SRAM
store rewriting mapped instruction descriptor or permissions
review.test_execution: Performed by the performance agent and release integrator; this independent review does not relabel their results as an additional run.
review.cold_function_split: Reviewed v3 cpu_checkpointed extraction: rollback snapshot remains after fetch and before speculative PC update; diagnostic restores the same CPU; data abort preserves FAR/FSR before entering ABT; cpu_step returns false for every cold dispatch. No new continuing instruction class.

cold_transaction_review.production_selection: Rejected; not present in production. The final isolated Chrome comparison did not establish improvement.
changes: Extract the unchanged cpu_step rollback tail into a static cpu_checkpointed function.
Use noinline for compilers that support the GNU attribute, to avoid allocating the full rollback frame on the existing hot paths.
unchanged_semantics: Function is called at the same point after instruction fetch and after the two pre-existing fast paths.
Full CPU snapshot remains before speculative next_pc update.
Diagnostic stop records the instruction and restores the complete saved CPU without incrementing the instruction count.
Data abort restores the CPU, retains FAR/DFSR and enters ABT with the same link value.
Successful cold instruction commits next_pc, and successful/aborted retired instructions increment the same counter.
cold_transaction_review.source_comparison: The extracted body is identical statement-for-statement to the previous cpu_step tail.

final_production.retained_change: The scheduler test adds dependent instruction, interrupt/mode/ISA transition, MMIO fetch, self-modifying code, SRAM mirror and page-table mutation regressions.

gcc_portability_review.method: Static cross-review only; no additional test matrix run.
gcc_portability_review.tools/checkpoint-replay.c: The unconditional return is placed on a separate line after the fclose failure check. File-read checks, close handling and returned status are unchanged.
gcc_portability_review.tests/checkpoint.c: Capture immutable per-model ram_bytes, check the lower wire-layout bound and upper backing-array bound before any size subtraction, and return the already-incremented failure count on a bad size. All later offsets use the same captured RAM size. This prevents unsigned offset underflow without suppressing a failure or changing core checkpoint behavior.
gcc_portability_review.validation_provenance: The performance agent reports GCC 13 reference 16/16 and ASan+UBSan 16/16, plus a focused checkpoint rerun after the guard change; these are not relabeled as independent runs.
